title: A locally finitely presented limit of closed-immersion systems eventually equals a stage
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces is a representable morphism whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $B$ be an algebraic space, let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, and let $(C_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system over $B$ whose transition morphisms are closed immersions. Assume every $C_i$ is quasi-compact, every $C_i\to B$ is locally of finite type, and the limit $C=\varprojlim_i C_i$ exists in algebraic spaces over $B$. If $C\to B$ is locally of finite presentation, then there exists $i_0\in I$ such that the canonical projection $C\to C_i$ is an isomorphism for every $i\geq i_0$.

source.place: Tag 0828 (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), clause (3), with Y equal to the limit X

proof.text: Choose $a\in I$ and restrict to $I_{\geq a}$. This tail is nonempty and directed. It has the same limit: a compatible tail cone extends uniquely to an index $k$ by choosing $j\geq a,k$ and composing its $j$-component with $C_j\to C_k$; a common upper bound proves independence of $j$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence] to $C\to C_a\to B$. The composite is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis and $C_a\to B$ is locally of finite type, so $C\to C_a$ is locally of finite presentation.

By [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement], choose an affine scheme $U_a$ and a representable surjective etale atlas $U_a\to C_a$. For $i\geq a$ set $U_i=C_i\times_{C_a}U_a$. These are schemes closed in $U_a$, by the assumed scheme-test definition of closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $j\geq i\geq a$, $U_j=C_j\times_{C_i}U_i$ is the base change of the closed immersion $C_j\to C_i$ along the scheme $U_i\to C_i$, so the same scheme-test definition makes the transition $U_j\to U_i$ a closed immersion. The affine-quotient clause of [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes every $U_i$ affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Also $U_i\to U_a$ is locally of finite type: on affine opens its ring map is a quotient, generated as an algebra by the empty set [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0828(3), affine surjective etale chart; Tag 03H6 (spaces-properties-lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover)

proof.text: The scheme-test definition of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes every transition affine: every affine scheme test has a closed, hence affine, scheme source. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to this system. Its sheaf limit is a limit in algebraic spaces over $B$ and is therefore canonically the given $C$. Its projection to $C_a$ is affine, so $U=C\times_{C_a}U_a$ is an affine scheme. The same cited node gives $U\cong\varprojlim_{i\geq a}U_i$. Scheme objects are the representable sheaves $h_T$ [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]: a natural transformation $h_T\to h_U$ is determined by its value on $1_T$, namely a scheme map $T\to U$, and naturality recovers composition with that map. Thus the same cone is also a scheme limit.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with property locally of finite presentation to $C\to C_a$, using target chart $U_a\to C_a$ and the identity scheme chart of $C\times_{C_a}U_a=U$. Step 1 supplies its hypothesis, and step 3 supplies that $U$ is a scheme. It follows that $U\to U_a$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0828(3), finite presentation on the affine chart; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0410 (lemma-finite-presentation-local)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-limit-lfp-stabilization] with scheme base $U_a$ and system $(U_i)_{i\geq a}$. Step 2 gives quasi-compact stages, closed immersion transitions and locally finite type structure maps. Steps 3 and 4 give its scheme limit and locally finite presentation of the limit over $U_a$. Thus there is $i_0\geq a$ such that the canonical $U\to U_i$ is an isomorphism for every $i\geq i_0$.

source.place: Tag 0828(3), reduction to affine schemes; limits.tex Tag 081B (lemma-finite-type-eventually-closed), (3)

proof.text: Fix $i\geq i_0$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $U_i\to C_i$ is representable surjective etale, and the pullback of $C\to C_i$ along it is $U\to U_i$. For any scheme $T\to C_i$, the scheme $T\times_{C_i}U_i\to T$ is surjective etale, hence an fppf cover [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fppf-site]. The isomorphism $U\to U_i$ gives exactly one lift to $C$ on this cover and on its double overlap. The two restricted lifts therefore agree and glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom for $C$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Consequently every $T\to C_i$ has exactly one lift to $C$, naturally in $T$. The resulting inverse natural transformation proves $C\to C_i$ an isomorphism.
